clue.text: Trendy river vessel diverts semiaquatic animals

parts.note: trendy means hip, fashionable
the Po is the great river of northern Italy
a pot is a cooking vessel
to divert someone is to entertain or amuse them

explanation.surface: A fashionable riverboat entertains a herd of large wallowing beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diverts' looks like the verb of the sentence steering the boat, but it means entertains.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippos spend their days half-submerged in rivers and lakes, so they are the classic semiaquatic mammals.

clue.text: Most important, so looked up to by everyone else

definitions.text: so looked up to by everyone else

explanation.surface: Someone at the top of the tree, admired by all below.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is literal: whatever is tallest is looked up at by everyone lower down.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-ranking means supreme in importance; literally, the tallest thing is the one everyone else must look up at.

clue.text: Local fare that's never free for farmworker?

definitions.text: Local fare that's never free for farmworker?

parts.words: Local fare that's never free for farmworker?
parts.note: local here is a British pub; the fare is a cold plate of bread, cheese and pickle named after a farm labourer, and there is no such thing as a free midday meal

explanation.surface: Pub food a farm labourer always has to pay for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British for one's neighbourhood pub; the saying 'there's no such thing as a free lunch' explains 'never free'.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional British pub meal of bread, cheese and pickle, named for a farm labourer who would eat it at midday.

clue.text: Ignoring odd constituents, socially ingratiating

indicators.note: ignoring odd constituents means skip the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of socially and keep the even ones

explanation.surface: Someone who skips the awkward types and smarms around at parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd constituents' sounds like strange people, but means the odd-numbered letters of 'socially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unctuous or smarmy flattery is described figuratively as slippery and greasy.

clue.text: Bloody stupid fellow who's left school

indicators.note: stupid suggests the letters of Bloody are muddled into nonsense order

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a dim chap who has finished school.
explanation.definitionFit: A former pupil of a British school is called this, a fixed term for an alumnus.

clue.text: First drink disorderly parties endlessly provided

indicators.note: disorderly means the remaining letters of parties are jumbled
endlessly means the word parties loses its final letter

parts.note: provided means if, as in provided that

explanation.surface: The opening round of drinks at rowdy gatherings that never seem to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' trims the S of 'parties' to PARTIE, and 'disorderly' rearranges that to APERIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A light alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite, so the opening drink of the evening.

clue.text: Kind of clue that prevents complete satisfaction

definitions.text: Kind of clue that prevents complete satisfaction

parts.words: Kind of clue that prevents complete satisfaction
parts.note: a crossword clue left unsolved stops the solver from finishing the grid with full satisfaction

explanation.surface: A puzzle clue that spoils the pleasure of a finished crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue nobody has solved remains without a reply, which leaves a crossword incomplete.

clue.text: One crazy is restrained by practised lab worker

indicators.note: restrained by means the inner pieces are held within the word for practised

parts.note: practised means skilled, expert
the Roman numeral I is one
mental is a slang word for crazy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lunatic is held down by a skilled laboratory scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who carries out trials and tests, typically working in a laboratory.

clue.text: You and I riding a docked horse? Colt, perhaps

indicators.note: riding means the word for you and I sits on top of what follows, as a rider sits on a mount

parts.note: you and I together are we

indicators.note: docked means cut short, as a horse's tail is docked, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a pony is a small horse

explanation.surface: Two people mounted on a bobtailed pony, with a young horse in view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colt' looks like a young horse, fitting the scene, but here it is the Colt revolver.
explanation.definitionFit: Colt is a famous make of revolver, so a Colt is an example of a firearm.

clue.text: Game regarded as desirable, checked out on internet

parts.note: go is the Japanese board game of black and white stones
to ogle is to look at someone with desire

explanation.surface: Someone plays a game and eyes up a potential date, then researches them online.
explanation.definitionFit: Searching for something with the leading web search engine is now a verb meaning looked it up online.

clue.text: Former partner gets plenty, for instance

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
ample means plenty, more than enough

explanation.surface: A divorce settlement in which an ex-spouse receives a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case cited to illustrate something, a synonym.

clue.text: Nervous, extremely excited and giddy

indicators.note: extremely means take the extremes, the first and last letters, of both excited and giddy

explanation.surface: Someone is jittery, very keyed-up and light-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'excited' but asks for the first and last letters of 'excited' and of 'giddy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means tense and on edge, a synonym for anxious.

clue.text: Newspaper feature, something both amusing and arousing?

explanation.surface: A tabloid feature that is funny and titillating at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the phrase literally: a funny striptease, a 'comic' strip.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon sequence printed daily in a paper; read playfully, a humorous striptease would be both funny and sexy.

clue.text: To graduate thus with university, entering best possible first course

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: entering means the words for thus and university go inside the word for best possible

parts.note: top means best possible, as in top quality
so means thus

explanation.surface: Going to university to graduate with the best possible degree.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about academic achievement; 'first course' is not a university module but a starter.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter served at the opening of a meal, a classic example of soup on a menu.

clue.text: Drum produced by male twins?

indicators.note: twins means the word for male appears twice, a pair of identical copies

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, so tom can stand for male

explanation.surface: A drum made by a pair of identical boys.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom-tom is a tall, narrow drum played with the hands or sticks, a specific kind of percussion.

clue.text: Judge making marginal decisions in court

definitions.text: Judge making marginal decisions in court

parts.words: Judge making marginal decisions in court
parts.note: sounds like a lawyer splitting hairs in a courtroom, but the court is a tennis court and the margins are its boundary lines

explanation.surface: A judge who rules on fine points in a court of law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a legal setting; in tennis, the official watching the edges calls balls in or out.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, the official stationed by a boundary calls whether the ball landed in or out, literally decisions about the margins.

clue.text: Scan iris, scattered in other flowers

indicators.note: scattered means the letters of scan iris are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone examines an iris scattered among a bed of different blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Other' fits because the fodder contains an iris, itself a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Daffodils and jonquils belong to this genus of spring bulbs, flowers distinct from the iris in the clue.

clue.text: Vehicle hemmed in by jeep and a cart

indicators.note: hemmed in by means the answer sits enclosed within the run of words jeep and a cart

explanation.surface: Some vehicle squeezed between a jeep and a cart in traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: A PANDA CAR is old British slang for a small police patrol car, once painted in blue and white panels.
explanation.definitionFit: A British police patrol car, so a kind of motor vehicle.

clue.text: Father breaks fast in church office

indicators.note: breaks means the word for father splits open the word for fast

parts.note: pacy means fast, quick
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A priest ends a religious fast while serving in a church role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like a religious abstinence, fitting the church scene; it is the adjective for speedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The position of Pope, head of the Catholic Church, is an ecclesiastical office.

clue.text: Completed and mounted, following directions

indicators.note: following means the word for mounted comes after the directions

parts.note: south, east, west and north are four compass directions
mounted means up, as on horseback

explanation.surface: A horse rider has finished the ride and got in the saddle as told.
explanation.walkthrough: The four compass points S, E, W and N are arranged here as a word; UP is placed after them because of 'following'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal that is sewn up is settled and finished, an idiom for concluded.

clue.text: One rascal under pressure in boat

indicators.note: under means, in this down clue, the other pieces sit beneath the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
the Roman numeral I is one
a rogue is a rascal

explanation.surface: A scoundrel feeling the strain while out on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow canoe hollowed from a single tree trunk, used in the Caribbean and Americas.

clue.text: In role of ruler, initiating inquiry

explanation.surface: A monarch begins a royal investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, the answer means 'in the role of monarch'; whole, it means putting a question.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, acting in the capacity of a monarch; read as one, posing a question or making a request.

clue.text: What's a sort of special cover, containing down?

definitions.text: What's a sort of special cover, containing down?

parts.words: What's a sort of special cover, containing down?
parts.note: down here is soft feathers, not a direction, and the special cover is one fitted over a bed cushion stuffed with them

explanation.surface: A riddle about some unusual covering that holds something down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' tempts as a direction or as a crossword clue; it is the fine feathers used to stuff bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A removable fabric sleeve goes over the soft cushion for your head, which is often filled with feathers.

clue.text: Standard covers one or two

indicators.note: covers means the standard word wraps around the one

parts.note: par is the standard, as in up to par
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A rule that applies to one thing or a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple of matching items forms a set of two, a synonym.

clue.text: River flanked by excellent piece of farmland

indicators.note: flanked by means the river letter has the word for excellent on either side

parts.note: ace means excellent

explanation.surface: A river bordered by superb farmland.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of land area traditionally used for fields, roughly 4,047 square metres.

clue.text: Guns producing shots hitting more than one target

definitions.text: shots hitting more than one target

explanation.surface: Weapons that fire shots striking several targets at once.
explanation.walkthrough: In billiards, a cannon is a shot where the cue ball strikes two other balls in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Large artillery pieces; and in billiards, strokes where the cue ball strikes both object balls.

clue.text: Very keen sinologist finally getting into ancient Chinese text

indicators.note: getting into means the final letter goes inside the text's name

parts.note: the I Ching is the ancient Chinese book of divination

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word sinologist

explanation.surface: An eager scholar of China finally starts reading a classic Chinese book.
explanation.definitionFit: Being eager to do something is idiomatically described as longing or impatient to get going.

clue.text: Place for spending a lot — or twopence?

definitions.text: Place for spending a lot — or twopence?

parts.words: Place for spending a lot — or twopence?
parts.note: a place where shoppers spend freely; but in British slang to spend a penny is to use the lavatory, so twopence suggests a public convenience in a mall

explanation.surface: Where people go to spend lots of money, or just a couple of pennies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spend a penny' is British slang for going to the toilet; shopping malls are noted places to find public conveniences.
explanation.definitionFit: A mall or complex of stores where people go to buy things.
